messages:
alisa: quick heads-up — ran a small sanity bakeoff for the new reranker (red-rerank-v2-ptq) on the small holdout, saw a ~0.9% MRR@10 drop versus float; NDCG@10 roughly flat. wondering if query stitching or doc truncation changed.
marco: where are the artifacts?
alisa: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/runs/1777777777 — summary below. short: model is smaller after PTQ, latency good, quality slightly down on MRR.
sanjay: is that statistical or obvious? what's the sample size?
alisa: holdout=2k queries (prod-ish mix), bootstrap CI looks borderline. i'll paste the run summary.
eval-bot: Run 1777777777 finished — metrics (holdout_small): NDCG@10: 0.624 -> 0.623 (-0.16%), MRR@10: 0.412 -> 0.408 (-0.97%), p-value(bootstrap)=0.08, n=2000. artifacts: /runs/1777777777/metrics.json
eva: can you paste the eval config? curious about stitch mode + doc truncation.
alisa: here's the CLI that launched it:
```
python eval.py --model red-rerank-v2-ptq --holdout holdout_small --stitch_mode concat --query_prefix "q:" --doc_trunc 1024 --batch 64 --tokenizer_normalize true
```
alisa: quick note — our quantization pipeline added a tokenizer whitespace-normalize step to fix OOV behavior; that might change how we stitch query+context.
marco: ah — so tokens shift and rank ordering changes slightly. did you try running float model with the new tokenizer normalize=true to isolate quantization effect?
alisa: not yet. i only ran PTQ model with the new tokenizer. good point.
sanjay: also check whether "concat" vs "delimiter" stitch changes example ordering. i've seen subtle NDCG differences when query+passage punctuation gets merged.
eva: agree. propose ablation: (1) float vs ptq with identical tokenizer_normalize=true, (2) stitch_mode concat vs delimiter, (3) doc_trunc 512/1024/2048. small runs (n=2k) each.
alisa: plan sounds good. i'll kick off (1) and (2) today.
marco: i'll diff tokenization outputs for a random 500 queries to see example-level flips. quick awk/py script should do.
sanjay: i'll run bootstrap resample (10k iters) to get tighter CI and compute pairwise example flips + mean delta distribution.
eva: i'll update the eval harness to log tokenized lengths and stitch preview for the top 20 flipped queries so we can triage.
alisa: quick triage note — one flipped example looked like: query "how to reset API key" + doc header "API keys — Reset & Rotate" got tokenized to fewer tokens after normalize, which pushed a different doc up.
marco: can you paste small sample of tokenization diff?
alisa: sure, from sample:
```
# raw -> normalized
"API keys — Reset & Rotate" -> "api keys - reset & rotate"
# token lists
raw: ["API","keys","—","Reset","&","Rotate"]
norm: ["api","keys","-","reset","&","rotate"]
```
marco: ok that single char change could affect subword boundaries in some tokenizers. likely explains small movement.
sanjay: still — <1% MRR is small but could be meaningful for production. we need to decide acceptance thresholds. what's current SLA?
eva: threshold for model promotion: MRR drop <=0.5% for small holdout, OR show no significant p-value <=0.05. product asked for conservative rollout.
alisa: noted. i'll try to reproduce float-with-new-tokenizer and ptq-with-old-tokenizer to isolate.
marco: if tokenizer-normalize is the culprit, maybe we add a deterministic normalizer in preproc before promotion and document it. also add unit tests around tokenization for anchor queries.
sanjay: for the ablation results, i'll prepare a one-page summary with example flips + bootstrap CI. include ndcg/mrr and topk flip counts.
eva: timeline?
alisa: i'll have runs + rough numbers by EOD today (kicking off now), sanjay should have bootstrap by tomorrow morning, marco token diffs in a few hours, eva will wire up logging. we'll reconvene in this thread once we have numbers.
marco: thanks — also flagging to infra: if we're running many small evals, can we get a short queue on the eval cluster? @eng-infra FYI.
(eval-bot reaction: :eyes:)
alisa: thanks all. leaving notes in run artifact. will post updated metrics when done. :thumbsup:
